title: Package the existing web app as an Android APK

requirements.text: Add an Android build wrapper for the existing React frontend so the project can be built and distributed as a signed Android .apk.
acceptanceCriteria: Repository contains Android wrapper project/config committed alongside the existing frontend.
A developer can run documented commands to generate a debug APK locally.
A developer can generate a release APK (signed) using documented environment variables/keystore inputs without modifying source code.

requirements.text: Ensure Internet Identity authentication works from the Android app context by handling login flow in a way compatible with Android WebView/app wrapper (e.g., opening the identity provider in an external browser/custom tab and returning to the app), without changing the immutable Internet Identity hook files.
acceptanceCriteria: User can log in and log out successfully on Android build (no blank window / blocked popup during login).
No edits are made to any immutable paths listed in SYSTEM_CONTEXT (including frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.ts and frontend/src/hooks/useActor.ts).

requirements.text: Add concise build documentation to the repo describing prerequisites and step-by-step instructions to produce debug and release APK artifacts for the app.
acceptanceCriteria: Documentation includes required tooling (Android Studio/SDK/Java version) and exact commands to build.
Documentation includes configuration steps for release signing and where the resulting APK outputs are located.

constraints: Do not modify any files under frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.ts, frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.tsx, frontend/src/hooks/useActor.ts, frontend/src/main.tsx, or frontend/src/components/ui (immutable paths).
Backend must remain a single Motoko actor in backend/main.mo; do not introduce additional backend services.
Do not introduce third-party authentication providers; Internet Identity remains the only auth method.
nonGoals: Adding push notifications, deep linking features beyond what is strictly necessary for authentication return, or real-time messaging.
Migrating to a different frontend framework (e.g., Next.js) or backend language.
